name: ITC Limited
line: Diversified Indian company: FMCG, cigarettes, agri-business and paperboards

cmd.label: ITC annual report 2026: Board of Directors

brief.t: One of India's biggest companies, with businesses in FMCG (foods, personal care, stationery), cigarettes, agri-business and paperboards.
Led by Chairman & Managing Director Sanjiv Puri, who has been Chairman since May 2019.
FY 2025-26 standalone net profit was ₹20,286 crore.
Q2 FY27 profit fell about 20% because of much higher cigarette taxes, while non-cigarette FMCG grew 19%.
Its FMCG brands (Aashirvaad, Sunfeast, Bingo!, Classmate and more) reach about 28 crore households.

timeline.t: Founded as the Imperial Tobacco Company of India.
Diversified into hotels, paperboards, agri-business and packaged foods.
Hotels business demerged into ITC Hotels Ltd.
Acquired the Century Pulp and Paper business.

model.how: ITC earns most of its profit from cigarettes, and reinvests that cash to build FMCG brands, agri-business and paper and packaging. Its strategy is to grow non-cigarette businesses so the company depends less on tobacco.
flow: Buys crops (wheat, tobacco, spices) from farmers
Makes foods, cigarettes, paper and packaging
Sells through a vast distribution network
Profit after costs, excise duty and tax

industry.regulator: Several: FSSAI (foods), tax authorities (cigarette excise), environmental regulators (paper)
points: Cigarette taxes have a big effect on ITC's profits.
In foods and personal care, ITC competes with HUL, Nestlé and Britannia.
Big interview theme: ITC's shift from tobacco to FMCG.

people.name: Sanjiv Puri
people.note: Joined ITC in 1986; also a former President of CII.

points.t: Standalone net profit ₹4,137 cr, down 20.1%, as higher cigarette taxes hit earnings.
Non-cigarette segment revenue grew 18% and segment results 24%.

numbers.say: ITC is reducing its reliance on cigarettes: its other businesses grew results 24% last quarter even as cigarette profits fell.

rivals.note: ITC competes in different industries, so compare business by business.

network.local: ITC's agri-business works with farmers across India, and its foods are sold in shops across Punjab and North India.

csr.t: ITC's CSR and sustainability work includes watershed development, afforestation, livestock development and women's empowerment, mainly in its agri-business areas.

s.t: Non-cigarette results up 24% in Q2 FY27

w.t: Profit still depends heavily on cigarettes

o.t: Large FMCG market; 30+ brands reaching 28 crore households

t.t: Strong FMCG rivals like HUL and Nestlé

bcg_note: ITC is a classic BCG example: Cigarettes act as the cash cow funding FMCG-Others (a growing question mark/star). We don't plot exact market shares because ITC doesn't publish them.

glossary.FMCG: Fast-Moving Consumer Goods: everyday products like soap, tea, biscuits, sold quickly at low prices.
glossary.Revenue from operations: Money earned from selling products and services, before costs.
glossary.Net profit: What is left after all costs and taxes.
glossary.EBITDA margin: Operating profit before interest, tax and depreciation, as a % of sales. Shows how efficiently the core business runs.
glossary.Underlying sales growth: Sales growth after removing one-off effects (like acquisitions or tax changes). Shows real demand.
glossary.Underlying volume growth: Growth in the number of units sold, not just higher prices. The best sign of real consumer demand.
glossary.Distribution reach: How many shops and outlets stock the company's products.
glossary.General trade: Small neighbourhood kirana shops, the backbone of FMCG sales in India.
glossary.Modern trade: Supermarkets and organised retail chains like DMart or Reliance Smart.
glossary.Quick commerce: 10–30 minute delivery apps like Blinkit, Zepto and Swiggy Instamart.
glossary.Premiumisation: Consumers moving to higher-priced, better products, which raises profit per unit.
glossary.Brand equity: The value a brand adds because people know, trust and prefer it.
glossary.Demerger: Separating one business into a new, independent company.
glossary.Excise duty: A tax on making certain goods, such as cigarettes. It is collected by the company and paid to the government.
glossary.Segment: A separate business line reported on its own in the company's results.
glossary.Attrition: The % of employees who leave in a year.
glossary.Dividend: Part of the profit paid to shareholders, per share.
glossary.BRSR: Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report: an official yearly report on people, environment and governance that big listed companies must publish.

Finance.tip: Know revenue, profit and margin, and why volume growth matters more than price growth.

Marketing.tip: Pick one brand you use, know its target customer, and suggest one idea to grow it.

HR.tip: FMCG companies value leadership and frontline sales talent. Talk about building capability in sales teams.

Sales.tip: Expect 'How will you increase sales in a town where our brand is weak?' Talk about outlets, displays and schemes.

Operations.tip: Talk about reducing stock-outs and wastage across many small shops.

Finance.q: Why did ITC's profit fall in Q2 FY27 even though revenue rose?
Finance.a: Gross revenue rose mainly because of higher cigarette excise duty collected, but cigarette profits fell 27%, so overall profit dropped about 20%.

Finance.q: What is the difference between gross and net revenue at ITC?
Finance.a: Gross revenue includes excise duty collected for the government; net revenue removes it, so net revenue shows the real business.

Marketing.q: Pick one ITC food brand and suggest how to grow it.
Marketing.a: For example Aashirvaad or Sunfeast: define the target customer and suggest one quick-commerce or regional campaign idea.

Marketing.q: How can ITC compete with HUL and Nestlé?
Marketing.a: Use its agri sourcing strength, strong distribution and fast innovation in foods.

HR.q: ITC runs very different businesses. How would you build a common culture?
HR.a: Shared values, cross-business rotations for trainees, and common leadership programmes.

Sales.q: How would you push a new ITC snack in small towns?
Sales.a: Small price packs, retailer schemes, in-store visibility and sampling at schools and fairs.

Operations.q: How does ITC's agri-business help its foods business?
Operations.a: It sources crops like wheat directly from farmers, ensuring quality and cost control for brands like Aashirvaad.

Other.q: What do you know about ITC?
Other.a: A diversified company in FMCG, cigarettes, agri and paper, led by Sanjiv Puri; FY26 net profit ₹20,286 cr.

common.a: Sanjiv Puri is Chairman & Managing Director.
Aashirvaad, Sunfeast, Bingo!, Classmate, Yippee! or Fiama. Say why you like one.
Use the 'Why us?' draft and add your own reason.

interview.why_us: ITC is transforming itself: its non-cigarette businesses grew results 24% last quarter, and its 30+ FMCG brands reach about 28 crore households. Working across foods, agri and packaging gives a young professional unmatched variety. I want to be part of this transformation and contribute to [your role] at one of India's most diversified companies.
ask: Which FMCG categories is ITC betting on next?
How do trainees move across ITC's businesses?
How is ITC using AI-led consumer insights in product development?

gd.for: Higher taxes reduce smoking and improve health.
gd.against: Very high taxes can push illegal trade and hurt farmers.

gd.for: ITC uses cash from one business to grow others.
gd.against: Investors often prefer focused companies; ITC demerged hotels.

avoid: Don't say ITC still runs hotels directly; ITC Hotels is now a separate company.
Don't talk only about cigarettes; show you know the FMCG brands.
Don't confuse gross revenue (with taxes) and net revenue.
